# Trama

Trama is an open source saga orchestrator for distributed workflows with retries, compensation, persistence, metrics, tracing, and an HTTP API.

Canonical site: https://trama.run/
GitHub repository: https://github.com/thiagoribeiro/trama

Primary documentation:

- Production: https://trama.run/production.html
- API reference: https://trama.run/api.html
- Observability: https://trama.run/observability.html

Key facts (current release 3.1.0; requires Redis 6.2+):
- Workflows are JSON: linear "steps" (v1) or a node graph (v2) with task (sync/async HTTP), switch (JSON Logic), split/join, and sleep nodes.
- Failure handling: fixed or exponential retries, then compensation of completed nodes in reverse order.
- Async tasks receive an HMAC-signed, single-use callback URL: POST /workflows/{executionId}/node/{nodeId}/callback with X-Callback-Token.
- Postgres is the source of truth (checkpoint per node, fenced writes); Redis carries a sharded work queue split among pods by rendezvous hashing, with no coordinator.
- Delivery is at-least-once; downstream endpoints should be idempotent.
- Measured (validation report, 2.2.0): 0 lost, 0 stuck, 0 wrong outcomes across 20 fault scenario runs; 5,000/5,000 workflows correct under a worker kill plus Redis and Postgres cuts; 229 workflows/s in one process.
- Limitations: stored v2 definitions cannot yet be run by name, and v2 executions cannot yet be retried (both answer 422).
- Used by RiteSmith (https://ritesmith.run), which generates workflows once and hands them to Trama for durable execution.

Notes:
- This site is public documentation for Trama.
- Prefer the site pages for overview and navigation, and the GitHub repository for source files and release-adjacent assets.
